action.rationale: Root is a dummy node used to hold the world model and branch alternatives.
action.title: DUMMY_ROOT_NO_ACTION

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Intel XPU/Triton should map tl.dot fp16 to XMX/DPAS-like paths when tile shapes align, but C=32, N=16, hidden=128 are small and launch/tile overheads matter.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Overall block has meaningful dense linear compute, but attention uses many tiny 16x16 windows and the MLP has narrow 32-to-128-to-32 projections.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Small reductions and many windows may underutilize matrix hardware if mapped too granularly.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input/output tensor is about 29.5M fp16 elements, roughly 59 MB per full read or write. Eager reference materializes LN, qkv, attention, MLP intermediates and performs window reshape/permute views plus contiguous operations.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Excess intermediate tensors or extra NHWC/window-format conversions can dominate despite moderate arithmetic intensity.

register_pressure.notes: Per-window resident data are small for attention, but holding 16 tokens by 32 channels plus qkv, attention logits/probs, and MLP hidden 16x128 can become register-heavy.
register_pressure.risk: Monolithic fusion can spill or reduce occupancy, especially if softmax and MLP hidden activations are retained simultaneously.

nodes.notes:
1) Classification: mixed transformer block: tokenwise LayerNorm/linear/GELU, windowed dense attention with softmax, residual adds, and dense layout transforms. Outputs are NHWC fp16, reductions occur over C for LN, in_features for linear layers, N=16 for attention softmax; accesses are dense with affine window indexing, no sparse data-dependent indexing except fixed rpe lookup already gathered.
2) Canonical math: for each token, u=LN_C(x); per 4x4 window, Q,K,V=u*Wqkv+b, A=softmax((Q/sqrt(32))K^T+rpe), a=proj(A V); y=x+a; z=LN_C(y); output=y+fc2(GELU(fc1(z))). Windows and tokens are independent except within each 16-token attention window; LN and MLP are token-independent.
3) Layout/access: x and output are contiguous NHWC shape [1,720,1280,32] fp16. Windows are logical [57600,16,32] with affine mapping from NHWC; weights are contiguous PyTorch linear layout [out,in] for qkv [96,32], proj [32,32], fc1 [128,32], fc2 [32,128]; rpe is [1,1,16,16]. Weight reuse is high globally; per-program reuse depends on tiling.
4) Bottleneck regimes: eager/compile regime likely launch and intermediate-memory dominated; attention-only regime likely latency/register dominated because N=16 softmax is tiny; MLP regime likely small-GEMM compute plus bandwidth for hidden activations; monolithic regime likely register/occupancy limited; large-fixed-image regime benefits from persistent streaming across 921600 tokens and 57600 windows.
5) Knobs: decomposition granularity, programs per window vs token tile, C/hidden tile sizes, fp32 vs fp16 accumulation for LN/softmax/dot, approximate vs exact GELU, intermediate buffer layout, qkv/proj/MLP staging, number of kernels, and whether to specialize hard for B=1,H=720,W=1280,C=32,Wh=Ww=4.
6) Skeleton: load token/window tile, compute LN statistics in fp32, apply affine LN and linear weights, compute window attention logits with rpe, stable softmax, multiply V, project and residual store; second phase computes LN2, fc1, GELU, fc2, residual. Registers should hold per-token vectors and small attention matrices; shared/local memory only if needed for window reuse or hidden tiling; no inter-program sync.
7) Candidate families: window-local resident cell minimizes global intermediates but risks spills; component-wise staged pipeline is easier and uses dense tensors but writes intermediates; token/MLP-centric path targets the largest FLOP component while leaving attention reference initially.

action.description: Implement a custom Triton path for norm1, qkv, 4x4-window attention, projection, reverse window placement, and first residual; keep the LN2/MLP path using existing PyTorch modules for the first experiment.
action.rationale: The W-MSA path contains awkward tiny-window attention, qkv/proj linears, and layout transformations that PyTorch eager handles with multiple kernels and intermediates. A custom path can remove reshape/materialization overhead while keeping the large MLP path correct and simple.
action.title: Custom W-MSA residual path

nodes.choice: Start with the window-attention half of the block

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Window size N=16 and channel C=32 are fixed, which allows a specialized small attention kernel; qkv/proj are small dense products repeated over 921600 tokens.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Window size 4x4 and C=32 are small but manageable. A partial attention implementation can validate XPU Triton dot/softmax behavior before attempting end-to-end fusion.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Replacing only window attention can still avoid some permute/view and small-op overhead while leaving MLP to stable library kernels. It has less intermediate traffic than a failed full custom pipeline.

register_pressure.notes: Attention path still has QKV/projection small GEMMs and softmax, but avoids the 16x128 MLP hidden activation in Triton. This is a safer isolation target after the full-block SIGSEGV.

nodes.notes:
CURRENT: This open family targets only the W-MSA residual path and leaves the feed-forward half unchanged. The failed full-block result makes this a better next experiment because it isolates the attention-specific kernels.
UPDATE_BELIEF: Confidence increases relative to the full staged approach because the crash likely came from over-combining several risky kernels. next bet: implement a conservative attention-only replacement with minimal temporary buffers and a PyTorch fallback for any unsupported shape.
SELF_CHECK: This sibling excludes MLP-first and full-block ownership because it specifically chooses attention as the first custom Triton surface.

action.description: Implement a custom Triton path for norm2, fc1, GELU, fc2, and second residual over token tiles; keep the attention path as the reference implementation for the first experiment.
action.rationale: The MLP has the largest dense arithmetic share, approximately two 921600-token projections through hidden=128, and PyTorch eager materializes norm2 and hidden activations. A custom token-tile path can fuse reductions, activation, and residual logic around the dense products.
action.title: Custom feed-forward residual path

nodes.choice: Start with the feed-forward half of the block

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: The 32-to-128-to-32 MLP has dimensions better suited to dense dot hardware than the 16x16 attention softmax, but tile shape must expose enough tokens per program to use XPU matrix engines well.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: The MLP has more regular GEMM-like structure than attention, but the small per-token fused implementation may not map as well as vendor/library linear layers on Arc.

memory_bandwidth.notes: MLP-first streams the full image tensor and hidden activation. It is simpler than full-block ownership but still materializes a large 128-channel hidden layer.

register_pressure.notes: The full-block failure implicates the 16x128 MLP Triton kernel as a possible source of register pressure or XPU codegen instability, so this path is downgraded slightly.

nodes.notes:
CURRENT: This open family would replace the feed-forward half first while leaving window attention unchanged. It remains plausible but is now less attractive because the failed full-block code included a high-pressure Triton MLP kernel.
UPDATE_BELIEF: The SIGSEGV does not prove MLP-first is wrong, but it increases suspicion around the fused LN+fc1+GELU+fc2 kernel shape. next bet: keep as a backup if attention-only fails or if implemented with a more conservative two-kernel linear/GELU split.
SELF_CHECK: This sibling excludes attention-first and full-block ownership because it chooses the MLP as the first custom Triton surface.

action.description: Implement an end-to-end Triton version of the full block as a small sequence of specialized kernels: attention-residual stage followed by feed-forward residual stage, with custom intermediate layouts chosen for contiguous streaming.
action.rationale: A complete custom staged block can eliminate most PyTorch eager overhead while avoiding the extreme register pressure of one monolithic kernel. It also permits direct control of intermediate layouts between window and NHWC forms.
action.title: End-to-end staged Triton block

nodes.choice: Replace the entire block using a staged custom decomposition

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Separating attention and MLP stages allows each to use tile shapes suited to its math: fixed 4x4 windows for softmax attention and wider token tiles for MLP.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Many small fixed-shape dot operations are theoretically compute-dense but may not map robustly to Intel Arc Pro B70 Triton codegen. The SIGSEGV indicates correctness/runtime stability dominates any expected compute benefit.

memory_bandwidth.notes: The design streams NHWC input and writes qkv, ctx, y, and out intermediates. It may still reduce some framework overhead, but materializing full qkv and context tensors at 720x1280 is bandwidth-heavy.

register_pressure.notes: The fused LN+QKV and MLP kernels use 16x32, 16x96, and 16x128 working sets. On Intel Arc/XPU Triton this likely creates excessive registers or spills and may contribute to instability.

nodes.notes:
CURRENT: does: Implements the entire simplified Swin block with custom Triton kernels for LN+QKV, attention context, projection+residual, and MLP+residual, with temporary qkv/context/y buffers. bottleneck: other/runtime stability first; if repaired, likely register pressure plus memory bandwidth from large intermediates.
FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent: yes. The code matches the intended end-to-end staged decomposition rather than only replacing attention or MLP.
UPDATE_BELIEF: The evaluation failed with SIGSEGV, so the prior expectation that a full staged custom block would be the best first target is strongly downgraded. The likely issue is an XPU Triton codegen/runtime problem triggered by aggressive small-matrix dot kernels and/or high register pressure. next bet: Pivot to a narrower partial replacement, preferably the attention path first, to isolate the risky kernels and reduce the blast radius while preserving PyTorch correctness for the MLP. A later full-block design should only be revisited after a passing partial Triton path proves the layout and dot shapes are stable.
PERF_GAP: expected_vs_observed: expected approximately 0.60x baseline latency, observed no valid latency because the process crashed with SIGSEGV. hypothesized_reason: the staged design overreached by combining multiple custom Triton kernels with high register pressure and large intermediates before validating Intel XPU support for the dot shapes and memory layout.
SELF_CHECK: This top-level family remains mutually exclusive with attention-first and MLP-first because it attempts ownership of the full block immediately.

action.description: Prototype a window-resident full-cell kernel family where each logical 4x4 window computes norm1, attention, projection, norm2, MLP, and both residuals with minimal global intermediates.
action.rationale: The fixed window size and small C make it tempting to keep one window's activations resident and avoid multiple full-tensor passes. This is the highest-upside path if register pressure remains acceptable.
action.title: Window-resident full-cell prototype

nodes.choice: Replace the entire block with a window-local resident computation

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: One program per window or per small group of windows naturally matches the 4x4 attention dependency, but may not expose enough matrix parallelism for hidden=128 MLP on Intel XPU.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: High data reuse inside a window, especially for qkv/attention/proj, but MLP compute may be too narrow per program.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: May fail to saturate XMX and rely on many small programs with high scheduling overhead.

memory_bandwidth.notes: The main upside is minimal global intermediate traffic: read input and weights, write final output, with few or no full activation temporaries.
memory_bandwidth.risk: If spilling occurs, local-memory traffic can become worse than explicit staged intermediates.

register_pressure.notes: Worst-case live state includes 16x32 activations, qkv, 16x16 attention, projected values, LN2 stats, and 16x128 MLP hidden fragments.
register_pressure.risk: Very high spill/occupancy risk; full fusion may be infeasible without splitting hidden or output channels.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: This sibling is a fundamentally different whole-window residency plan; it cannot be combined with staged-full, attention-first, or MLP-first siblings in one first implementation because it uses a different ownership model and avoids the staged intermediate interface.

kernel_summary: This is a fixed-shape fp16 simplified Swin block over NHWC [1,720,1280,32] with 57600 independent 4x4 windows, single-head N=16 attention, two LayerNorm reductions over C=32, dense qkv/proj linears, and an MLP 32->128->32. The primary opportunity is not a single large GEMM but removing PyTorch eager launch/intermediate overhead and specializing tiny window attention plus narrow tokenwise MLP for Intel XPU Triton. The main constraints are matching fp16 PyTorch numerics with fp32 LN/softmax-style accumulation, preserving NHWC/window indexing exactly, and balancing global-memory savings against register pressure from over-fusing attention and hidden=128 MLP state.
open_questions: Are input shape, batch size, C=32, hidden=128, window_size=[4,4], and shift_size=[0,0] guaranteed fixed for all evaluation cases, or must the implementation handle runtime variants?
What correctness tolerance is used, especially for LayerNorm accumulation order, GELU approximation, softmax stabilization, fp32 versus fp16 dot accumulation, and final fp16 rounding?
Does the evaluator include model construction/first-call JIT compilation time, or only warmed steady-state latency after Triton kernels are compiled?
How efficient is Intel XPU Triton tl.dot for small fp16 shapes such as 16x32 by 32x96 and token tiles by 32x128; does it reliably use matrix hardware?
Are temporary tensor allocations inside forward allowed without penalty, or should buffers be preallocated/cached as module attributes for stable performance?
Is performance compared against PyTorch eager only, torch.compile, or the best of both, and are all reference weights contiguous fp16 on xpu?
What are the Arc Pro B70 occupancy, maximum workgroup, local-memory, and register-spill characteristics for Triton kernels with 16x16 softmax and hidden=128 fragments?
